csharp: {folder, name}: makes a C# script `folder/<name>.cs` from a template (a class deriving from GameScript); returns {path, module}
why: The C# engine's scripts are C# files (docs/csharp-redesign.md, decided by the operator on 2026-11-26): script.new writes a .cs file where the Rust engine makes a Rust crate.

csharp: {path}: a C# script of the project (or any path in it); compiles the project's scripts, running none of them; returns {module, log}, or fails with the compiler's problems
why: As for script.new: script.build compiles the project's C# scripts with Roslyn where the Rust engine builds a crate to WebAssembly with cargo.

C# only. A C# script runs in the editor's process with no sandbox, so opening a project first asks the person before its scripts run (docs/csharp-redesign.md, "Scripts"); this is the command the editor's question and menu give the answer through. The Rust engine's WebAssembly scripts are sandboxed and need no such consent.
